exposure: Antenatal corticosteroids for an asymptomatic short cervical length
Antenatal corticosteroids for preterm labor symptoms
outcome: Optimal antenatal corticosteroid exposure (latency to delivery of <=7 days)
Receipt of initial or rescue antenatal corticosteroids within 7 days of a preterm delivery of less than 34 weeks' gestation
cohort: The study included 287 women with a previous spontaneous preterm birth and a singleton gestation who underwent serial cervical length assessment at a large academic tertiary medical center from 2011 to 2016.
finding: Women with a previous preterm birth who received antenatal corticosteroids for an asymptomatic short cervical length were significantly less likely to have optimal exposure (delivery within 7 days) and less likely to receive an initial or rescue course within 7 days of a preterm delivery of less than 34 weeks' gestation compared to women with preterm labor symptoms.
gest_age: Cervical length assessment after 24 weeks' gestation; preterm delivery less than 34 weeks' gestation (as an outcome measure).
